approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves task-local molecular graphs from scored observations, draws ranked breeding parents from greedy survivors, and constructs a complete surplus pool through crossover and ordinary graph mutations. Stable molecular identity and a final sulfur-signature gate admit only fresh unique offspring whose outside-envelope signatures do not exceed the per-signature maximum in their original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process on folded Morgan occurrence counts learns every earlier accepted raw score with adaptive normalization. Joint posterior function draws then choose the announced evaluation batch, and real accepted feedback immediately updates both survivors and the chronological learning archive.
approach.novelty: This full-pool generation-order control removes the composite posterior selector’s influence on successful evaluation choices while retaining its original computation and the sulfur gate. The first admitted members receive evaluation in their inherited generation order. The older control tested ungated pools; this tests the selector after sulfur admission changed the pool and ancestry. The pending siblings change predictive means or residual laws while retaining active predictive allocation, so they answer different questions.

observed_bottleneck: The unresolved limiting behavior is attribution of active composite posterior allocation on the changed sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180. Its complete actual summary.json/run.log panel has macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287, 0.583088384937917. All fifteen tasks finish with 300 accepted observations, batch ten and no external invalid/duplicate proposals; run logs retain the srun CPU-allocation warning alongside successful final receipts. Against ungated n-62daf219c70a the gate changes the mean by only +0.0007834645552323346, with seed changes +0.017686193676039963, +0.002307179813052951 and -0.01764297982339591, six endpoint gains/six losses/three ties. The gate rejects 130 positive-excess opportunities in 81 batches, so selector inputs and subsequent histories changed. Source inspection finds the original selector retained, but catalog composition remains needs_review. n-01b48dd09404’s exact full-pool generation-order control loses -0.12438789088524467 under the old ungated Parent, with thirteen losses and positive zaleplon seeds 0/1; it is conditional support, not measured current-Parent contribution. n-07dd356cb779’s exponential full-law change improves selected-stream prediction/local wins yet loses -0.032277693549492024; n-c8e2f3c42535’s scoped breeder control has more parent beats and improved selected-stream prediction yet loses -0.24467619681869301. These counterexamples require absolute outcome and complete endpoint evidence rather than predictive/local proxies.
hypothesis: Remove only active influence of composite posterior selector m-000000000005 at the successful full-pool allocation consumer: emit the first announced-batch-size valid unique sulfur-gate-admitted members in inherited generation order, retaining the entire inherited fresh pool and original accepted-only count-GP fitting, covariance, factorization and normal draws as passive computations, with inherited numerical-failure routing unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection remains valuable after sulfur admission: removal loses 0.128 mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights:
The joint posterior allocation still contributes substantially after sulfur admission changes the available pool and later ancestry. This is now measured under the current gated conditions, with exposure in every task and seed; the earlier ungated loss alone could not establish that. More novel cores, more new parent-beating cores and easier selected-stream prediction did not preserve absolute source quality or incumbent improvement. This rules out treating those local proxies, or the narrower seed-average dispersion, as sufficient evidence of useful exploration. The result concerns the whole successful allocation consumer and its total adaptive effect. It does not isolate a mean, fingerprint, normalization or residual constituent, show a sulfur interaction, or attribute the whole graph foundation.

Chemistry remains mixed. Fewer N-halogen structures coexist with more O-halogen and peroxide structures, while useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy alternatives and useful permitted sulfur remain. Some of the highest labels still belong to chemically doubtful output, including the cyclic-peroxide family in the sole improving endpoint. Those examples preserve exceptions without proving a chemical mediator, a universal liability penalty or a benefit from broader filtering. Passive alternatives have no new labels or continued ancestry. Current composition review, separate constituent and joint-interaction evidence, chemical mediation, partial alternative-lineage composition and full-history coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen matched task/seed runs completed with the full budget. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.468270, a paired loss of 0.128183. All three seed averages fell, by 0.20602, 0.07253 and 0.10599. Fourteen endpoints fell; the sole gain was zaleplon seed 1, from 0.474117 to 0.479919. The control emitted exactly the first ten admitted molecules from every one of 435 complete 160-member pools. The passive original selector chose a different set in every batch and strictly preferred another identity in 4321 of 4350 same-mask selections. There were no natural fallback, incomplete-pool or factorization failures. The entire original GP computation and sulfur rule remained present.

The control produced 634 parent-beating offspring versus 648, but only 155 sequential incumbent advances versus 255. Its average offspring score was 0.22594 versus 0.37205, and average best-generating-parent score 0.31170 versus 0.45530. It created more new typed/generic cores (2366/1815 versus 1820/1117), including more new parent-beating cores (325/229 versus 262/163). Fewer accepted sources later entered breeding (2038 versus 2469). Final-batch sources were censored for later reuse. Prospective prediction accuracy on the control's own accepted stream was better: unequal-label pair accuracy 0.771 versus 0.710 and mean within-batch Spearman 0.666 versus 0.526. Those are different selected streams; at the same actual identity the passive original mean is unchanged and its MSE contrast is zero.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive bonds, difficult connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry across divergent seed histories
molecular.overall_character: Node n-605c7a785b51 produces linked nitrile/azaaryl amines, fused aryl amides, large azaaryl/dicarbonyl assemblies, aryl cyclic amines and sulfoxides, connected nitrogen/dione rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Whole-trajectory diversity is moderate, with much narrower repeated leader families within seeds; distinct strings are not evidence of independent useful scaffolds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9437-0.9747 and aromatic-string incidence 0.6609-0.9724. These are fractions of molecules exhibiting text features, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Charged and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on all five objectives. This does not mean basic amines or potentially stereogenic graphs are absent. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2112 of 4350 Child optimizer observations, compared with 2455 Parent observations. Child has 397 observations with O-O bonds, 172 with N-halogen bonds, 517 with O-halogen bonds and 27 with S-halogen bonds; Parent counts are respectively 128, 786, 217 and 93. These classes overlap and are chemical flags, not measured stability. Lower N-halogen incidence coexists with higher O-halogen and peroxide incidence, so no global chemistry improvement follows. Sulfur-containing observations remain 1108 Child versus 1100 Parent; permitted local sulfur chemistry is not a whole-molecule plausibility guarantee. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak because recognizable medicinal motifs coexist with reactive local attachments, difficult ring geometry, tiny fragments and overgrown structures. All 15 Child and 15 authoritative published Parent trajectories were read completely. Each side has 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations; no path, task or paired seed is missing. All digest counters, counts, extreme scores and digest molecule/score/evaluation/source/seed tuples match the Child files. context.comparison has child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. Full trajectories establish seed endpoints; digest final_molecules are late proposals, not incumbents. Parent baseline is n-1744a1494180 under the supplied Research in Depth epoch-1 profile, 300 observations including ten initial and announced batches of ten. The measured macro values are Child 0.4682702139687083 and Parent 0.59645311428869, with paired delta -0.12818290031998167. Chemistry differences are own-stream descriptive associations under divergent feedback histories, not selector activation, a selector constituent contribution, a sulfur contribution or chemical mediation. Unlabelled passive pool alternatives have no invented score or ancestry here. The frozen catalog composition_status=needs_review at v-17b4d64669a7955c8e61ca7e remains unresolved by this report; whole-foundation, constituent, joint-interaction, mediation, partial L07 composition and full-history-processing gaps remain separate. Prior transferable gaps retain their original n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180 conditions, rather than becoming unconditional efficacy evidence. Complete paths, hashes, descriptor counts and cited example audits are in .slots/round-0027-slot-3/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. All cited complete SMILES are digest or trusted Child-search molecules; Parent chemistry is described from its published trajectories and original report.

per_task.generated_character: The median optimizer molecule has 25 heavy atoms versus Parent 24; the range is 1-52. Seed-0 and seed-2 leaders are 24-heavy-atom fused aryl nitrogen/carbonyl systems with methoxy, methyl, ether and fluoroaryl substitution. Seed 1 instead leads with a 25-heavy-atom nitrile-substituted pyridyl/phenyl pair linked through an NH group to an unsaturated cyclic peroxide bearing a fluoroethyl chain; it has three perceived rings. Ring and aromatic text incidences are 0.9598 and 0.9506. Recognizable aryl amides coexist with peroxide and constrained-ring relatives; ring richness does not establish routine synthesis.
liabilities: O-O bonds occur in 29 of 870 optimizer observations versus Parent 7; the strongest Child molecule contains one.
Small-ring unsaturation occurs in 216 Child observations versus Parent 64; this audit flags geometry for inspection, rather than declaring every flagged graph impossible.
Direct N-halogen incidence falls from Parent 275 to Child 35, but other liabilities persist; lower incidence alone is not score mediation.
missing_features: Stable, conventional alternatives to the unsaturated cyclic peroxide are incompletely represented at the very highest label; an ether analogue already scores well, so peroxide is not demonstrably required.
Chemically independent plausible realizations of the favorable aromatic/polar relationship and specified identity at stereogenic ring closures remain limited among leaders.

The nitrile/azaaryl cyclic-peroxide leader scores 0.4799190055245768, while a related cyclic ether with fluoromethyl scores 0.457118710172062. Both retain the linked aromatic/polar arrangement, so this does not isolate a peroxide benefit. An overgrown 52-heavy-atom aromatic/dione concatenation at the final evaluation scores 4.468139161298754e-17. Child endpoints for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.4137456434408254, 0.4799190055245768 and 0.40018522659086975; Parent endpoints are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. Parent leaders include an azaaryl N-hydroxy amide and an adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl system, whereas Child seed 1 reaches a distinct nitrile series and improves its measured endpoint. The association favors an appropriately sized multi-ring polar arrangement over isolated fragments or concatenation; it identifies no exact missing target group.

Long imine/polyene chains, N-O substituents and densely fused closures create stability and synthesis questions that aromatic SMILES labels cannot answer.
A 120-heavy-atom maximum shows substantial growth excursions; no fixed size cutoff or blanket polyene prohibition follows from these labels.
missing_features: Compact, chemically credible alternative connectivity preserving the aromatic and carbonyl/heteroatom relationships remains incompletely represented; extra rings and mass clearly do not close the observed Parent gap.

Routine substituent environments and accessible geometry are missing in some high-label structures; near-leading conventional ether/ketone chemistry is an explicit counterexample to universal reliance on reactive attachments.

per_task.generated_character: Median size is 33 heavy atoms versus Parent 29, with a 1-113 range. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1744a1494180 versus its current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a, on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective. No Child optimizer observation has an absolute outside-envelope sulfur centre, yet 93 of 4350 contain sulfur-halogen bonds, including high-scoring S-F or S-Br structures. A conventional methylthio analogue has a slightly higher label than its S-F relative. Other high-scoring families retain N-halogen, O-F, nitroso and N-S chemistry. The envelope is the exact declared n-93cd9a000278 neutral local condition; its source score effect is not transferred or pooled here. The broader local-bond gap was already recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. Current re-observation: n-605c7a785b51 versus n-1744a1494180 under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations per objective, announced batch ten, with unchanged inherited sulfur admission. Among 4350 accepted optimizer observations, Child has 397 O-O, 517 O-halogen, 172 N-halogen and 27 S-halogen incidences versus Parent 128, 217, 786 and 93. Counts overlap; the useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy analogues keep the concern local and environment dependent. These own-stream observations do not identify a selector constituent or chemical mediator.
transferable_gaps.gap: A narrow sulfur envelope leaves substantial environment-dependent sulfur and non-sulfur reactivity unresolved in emitted molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish intact functional-group environments and generate conventional alternatives preserving useful molecular arrangements. Treat a permitted local sulfur class as a narrow representation condition, not a safety, stability or synthesis certificate. Preserve useful thioethers, thiocarbonyls and oxides where feedback supports them. The observed chemistry neither proves that a broader filter improves scores nor attributes a residual motif to a specific component; inherited outside-envelope signatures remain allowed by the declared relative rule under other starting states. Preserve the original source/profile conditions when consuming this gap; the current output association adds no causal performance guarantee.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
